svg.title: Which Model, Which Store, Which Storage Mode?
svg.desc: A decision tree with three questions. The first asks what the model must optimise for: query simplicity for BI leads to a dimensional star schema; auditable history and many changing source systems leads to a data vault; a shared integration layer across domains leads to a canonical model. The second asks who consumes the physical layer: Spark and data engineering favour a Lakehouse over Delta tables, while T-SQL and multi-table transactions favour a Warehouse — both write Delta and both surface through a semantic model. The third asks how the semantic model should read the data, forking between Direct Lake, Import, and DirectQuery. A warning branch covers the Direct Lake trap in which basing a table on a SQL view silently forces every query into DirectQuery fallback.
svg.text: Warehouse (T-SQL, multi-table ACID) — Full T-SQL surface with multi-table transactions — still Delta underneath, still open in OneLake.Data Modelling in Microsoft Fabric

text.aria-label: What must the model optimise for?

svg.text: What must the model optimise for? — The root question: pick the modelling technique from the job the model has to do, not from habit.Data Modelling in Microsoft Fabric decision path — Define grain and history, Choose dimensional, vault, or canonical form, Publish governed semantic model

text.title: Data vault — Hubs, links, satellites — when auditable history across many volatile sources is the actual requirement.

text.aria-label: How should the semantic model read it?
text.title: How should the semantic model read it? — Third question: Direct Lake, Import, or DirectQuery — the mode determines refresh cost and freshness.
Dimensional / star schema — Facts at a declared grain plus conformed dimensions — the default when BI query simplicity is the goal.

text.aria-label: Trap: SQL views force DirectQuery fallback

svg.text: Trap: SQL views force DirectQuery fallback — In Direct Lake on SQL, a table based on a SQL view sends every query into DirectQuery fallback.⚠ Measures duplicated per report

Who consumes the physical layer? — Second question: Lakehouse or Warehouse — decided by engine and skills, not by storage format.In Atlas: select a choice → inspect evidence → drill into inputs, processing, outputs, example, controls, and risks.
Lakehouse (Spark over Delta) — Managed Delta tables queried by Spark and T-SQL, with no movement between the two.Fabric Atlas original · Microsoft Fabric implementation guidance
